title: Paley–Zygmund inequality
statement:
Let $Z$ be a real-valued random variable on a probability space that is almost surely nonnegative and has finite first and second moments $\E[Z]$ and $\E[Z^2]$, with $\E[Z] > 0$. Then for every $\theta$ with $0 \le \theta \le 1$,
\[
\Pr\bigl[\, Z > \theta\,\E[Z] \,\bigr] \;\ge\; \frac{(1-\theta)^2\,(\E[Z])^2}{\E[Z^2]}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: Z has finite second moment (Z^2 integrable)
replaced:
Let $Z \ge 0$ be a nonnegative random variable with finite first and second moments and
positive mean. For every $\theta$ with $0 \le \theta \le 1$,
\[
\Pr\bigl[\,Z > \theta\,\E[Z]\,\bigr] \ge \frac{(1-\theta)^2\,(\E[Z])^2}{\E[Z^2]}.
\]
